title: Degree-90 packed Round-2 tail
objective: Replace fixed modulo assignment for independent local Round-2 solves with a deterministic dynamic pthread work queue while preserving caller-order exact merge, transactional failure cleanup, forced-static equality, and non-pthread sequential behavior

oracles: forced generic FLINT order payload equality
exceptions: Extends the existing FLINT host adapter and packed fmpz representation primitive; no mathematical algorithm is selected by function name and exact generic FLINT remains the tested capability fallback.

handoff.summary: Independent immutable-source p-maximal solves now use a mutex-protected monotone pthread work queue while retaining fixed caller-order result slots and exact ordered HNF merge. A fatal local result closes the queue to new claims, all claimed work joins, and the caller clears every published slot. Thread creation failure reduces concurrency without losing work; mutex initialization failure uses the retained static scheduler; non-pthread Windows remains sequential. The quiet degree90 batch improved from 4.051s static to 3.923s dynamic with an identical canonical lattice.
risks: The fresh degree90 public path still exceeded 120 seconds after the native tail was reduced to 4.55 seconds. The censored diagnostic emitted no stage marker, so the remaining downstream merge/materialization/certification stage must be isolated with an externally bounded marker-emitting probe.
Native Windows FLINT intentionally uses the exact one-lane fallback because FLINT_USES_PTHREAD is false; it has correctness coverage but not the pthread performance capability.
Current performance receipts are Linux x64. Linux arm64, macOS arm64, and native Windows x64 remain integration CI requirements.
next_steps: Review and integrate the dynamic-queue commit range from the agent/nf-opt-round2-degree90 branch.
Profile the degree90 public path with an external process-group timeout and streaming stage markers to locate the downstream >120-second residual without repeating native work.
Rerun the registered sanitizer witness after integration so the newly enabled forced-static sanitizer half is included, then exercise the non-pthread fallback on native Windows CI.
